tweets.text:
🧠💡Mastering #GenerativeAI in 2025 ➡️The 9️⃣-Stage Journey⤵️
🎯Knowing #AI isn’t Enough👉 Building Responsible, Real-world-ready Systems is What Sets You Apart👌

1️⃣ Foundations of AI 🧠
↳ Clarify differences between AI, ML & DL
↳ Grasp key fundamentals: optimizers, activation functions, gradient descent

2️⃣ Data & Preprocessing 📊
↳ High-quality input = high-performance output
↳ Clean, normalize, tokenize, engineer & balance your datasets

3️⃣ Language Models (LLMs) 🗣️
↳ Study transformers, positional encoding, scaling laws
↳ Move beyond usage ➡️ understand the architecture

4️⃣ Prompt Engineering ⚙️
↳ Design effective prompts & structured chains
↳ Manage tokens, optimize for precision & clarity

5️⃣ Fine-tuning & Training 🛠️
↳ Apply PEFT, LoRA, RLHF
↳ Tune models efficiently with limited data

6️⃣ Multimodal & Generative Models 🔄 
↳ Integrate image, video, audio & cross-modal capabilities
↳ Explore diffusion models, captioning & multimodal search

7️⃣ RAG & Vector Databases 🔍
↳ Ground LLMs with external knowledge
↳ Work with Pinecone, FAISS, ChromaDB & more

8️⃣ Ethical & #ResponsibleAI ⚖️
↳ Address bias, ensure explainability
↳ Prioritize trust, governance & transparency

9️⃣ Deployment & Real-World Use 🚀
↳ From prototype to production
↳ Focus on APIs, scaling, inference, logging & usage controls

I am convinced we are doing AI coding wrong. Completely wrong in fact.

Humans need abstraction and code reuse to reduce costs and manage complexity. 

That is not true for AIs however. They can just brute force things. No reuse and abstractions needed.

So instead of trying to coerce AIs to "structure" their code for our own benefit, we should just let them do the thing they do best, generate whatever code they want. As long as it works, we should be happy.

It is a bit like organizing your email in folders vs using search.

Embrace the chaos!
